label: Marketplace / individual plan (Healthcare.gov or a state exchange)
note: Individual and family plans bought on an exchange run the calendar year. Your deductible and out-of-pocket maximum reset on January 1 regardless of which company issued the plan.
whereToCheck: Your Summary of Benefits and Coverage names the coverage period at the top.

label: Medicare (Part A / Part B)
note: Medicare deductibles are set per calendar year and reset on January 1. A Medicare Advantage or Part D plan attached to it follows the same calendar year.
whereToCheck: Your plan's Evidence of Coverage, or medicare.gov.

label: Employer plan on a January benefit year
note: Most employer-sponsored plans align their benefit year to January 1, which is why open enrollment usually lands in November. Confirm rather than assume — the insurer's name tells you nothing about this.
whereToCheck: Your benefits portal, or ask HR for the plan year start date.

label: Employer plan on a non-January benefit year
note: A large share of employers run their benefit year on their fiscal year instead — July 1 and October 1 are both common, and universities and school districts often start in the summer. Same insurer, different reset date, entirely different cost.
whereToCheck: Ask HR for the plan year start date, or read the coverage period on your Summary of Benefits and Coverage.

label: Student health plan
note: Student plans usually follow the academic year, commonly starting in August or September, and some run on a per-term basis.
whereToCheck: Your school's student health insurance page states the policy year.

label: COBRA continuation
note: COBRA continues your former employer's plan, so it keeps that employer's benefit year — and any deductible you already met this plan year normally carries over.
whereToCheck: Your COBRA election notice, or the former employer's HR.

label: Medicaid
note: Medicaid generally has no deductible and minimal cost sharing, so the plan-year reset rarely drives cost. Eligibility is redetermined on your own enrollment anniversary, which is not a deductible reset.
